title: rest: the cross-object `POST /batch` per-op exposure gate keys objects by name, so a legacy `ns__short` object addressed by its short name keeps the pass-through #27728/#27729 closed on the `/data` routes
body:
domain:server#3 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4czuTWNgKR22fKv7jia

Filing gate: ① product defect with a named fix site (`finding`, class b: code read, not measured). Rule level only.

**Found by:** the #27728/#27729 card thread and the contract review of PR #27897. Filed by `domain:server` seat 3.

## What is wrong

PR #27897 makes the `/data/:object` exposure gate (`enforceApiAccess` → `loadObjectItem`) read an object exactly as the data door does (`registry.getObject`, including the legacy `ns__short` resolution). A legacy-named object that someone addresses by its short name is then judged by its own `enable` settings (`apiEnabled`, `apiMethods`).

The cross-object `POST /batch` door's per-op gate (`packages/rest/src/batch-routes.ts`) still keys its object list by name, so the old short-name pass-through remains on that one door. This predates #27897, and #27897 does not make it worse. As far as we know, no shipped object carries a `__` name today.

## Expected

The per-op gate reads each op's object through the same read the `/data` gate now uses, and refuses it the same way. Pin it with a legacy-named object that is not exposed, addressed by its short name.

## Business reason

The data doors should all give one answer about whether an object is exposed. This is the last door that answers differently.

**Reader:** the `domain:server` lane seat. It is serial behind PR #27897, because it reuses the gate's read.

**Dedupe:** I searched "batch per-op gate short name ns__short exposure". #27711, #27728 and #27729 cover the import and data doors only.

Filed without `domain:*`; grading is triage's. Contract review suggests p3.

Blocked-by: #27897
